title: Zariski degree-zero comparison for a proper scheme over a henselian pair
statement: Let $(A,I)$ be a henselian pair [def-weil-pbc-henselian-terminology] and let $f:X\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ be a proper morphism of schemes [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions]. Let $Z=X\times_{\operatorname{Spec}A}\operatorname{Spec}(A/I)$ [def-pc-fibre-product], viewed as a closed subset of the underlying topological space of $X$ (the projection $Z\to X$ is a closed immersion, the base change of $\operatorname{Spec}(A/I)\to\operatorname{Spec}A$). For every sheaf of sets $\mathcal F$ on the underlying topological space of $X$, the restriction map $\Gamma(X,\mathcal F)\to\Gamma(Z,\mathcal F|_Z)$ is bijective, where $\mathcal F|_Z$ is the topological inverse image of $\mathcal F$ along the inclusion $i:Z\subseteq X$ [def-weil-pbc-topological-inverse-image], taken with values in sets: the sheafification [def-weil-pbc-sheafification] $\theta:i_p\mathcal F\to\mathcal F|_Z$ of the presheaf $i_p\mathcal F:U\mapsto\varinjlim_{V\supseteq U}\mathcal F(V)$ ($V$ open in $X$; colimit [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit] with coprojections $\iota^U_V$), and the restriction map is $s\mapsto\theta_Z(\iota^Z_X(s))$.

proof.text: The quotient-spectrum morphism q is a closed immersion, hence its base change i is a closed immersion. Mathlib Scheme.Pullback.range_fst and range_comap_of_surjective identify range(i) with f inverse-image of V(I), using ker(A to A/I) = I. This directly uses the fibre-product range API, without a separate tensor-product argument.

Apply the existing, proved Scheme.Hom.spectralSpace_and_isClosed_and_isConnected_inter to f and I. It packages the same integral Stein-factorization and connected-fibre quotient argument of the original steps 3 through 6. In particular X is spectral, and for each point x the irreducible closed subset closure{x} meets f inverse-image of V(I) in a connected nonempty set. The range identity of step 1 and commutativity of intersection give the spectral restriction hypothesis for range(i).

To retain exactly the unit along i, put D = range(i), let j:D to X be inclusion, and identify D homeomorphically with the domain of i. The induced equivalence of open-set categories preserves covers in both directions: the cover condition at a point and at its homeomorphic image coincide. Its induced sheaf equivalence S has a canonical natural isomorphism i_* = S followed by j_*; componentwise this is the identity on the same presheaf. These elementary constructions are proved locally, in the same universe Type u; no enlarged-universe restriction theorem is substituted for the required map.

Take the inverse mate alpha of the pushforward comparison under i inverse-image adjoint to i_* and j inverse-image adjoint to j_*. It is invertible because S and the ambient identity functor are equivalences. Mathlib unit_mateEquiv_symm identifies the unit along i with the unit along j followed by j_*(alpha) and the inverse of the pushforward comparison. Evaluate this equation at the top open. Apply the spectral closed-restriction theorem to D using step 2; the two remaining factors are components of isomorphisms and thus bijective. Their composite proves bijectivity of precisely the restriction unit written in the theorem.

split_report.summary: Proof written fresh from the Stacks proof of Tag 0A0B, in six steps: (1) Z = f^{-1}(V(I)) via the points of a fibre product and X spectral (094L); (2) reduction by 09ZG to connectedness of Z ∩ closure{x}; (3) replace X by a closed subscheme Y on closure{x} (01J3, existence only), Y proper over A; (4) Stein factorization of Y (03H2) and (B,IB) henselian (09XK); (5) the image T' of Y in Spec B is V(q) for a prime q and T' ∩ V(IB) = V(q+IB) is connected (09Y6); (6) Y_0 → V(q+IB) is surjective, closed, with connected fibres, so Y_0 is connected (0377). The step 'we may assume the fibres are geometrically connected' of the source is carried out over B. All Stacks tags verified in literature/stacks-project/tags/tags. Seven new nodes: three Mathlib leaves (094L, 0377, existence part of 01J3), four unsplit (09ZG for sheaves of sets, 03H2 over an affine base, 09XK, 09Y6). Statement kept; it now cites the definitions it uses (fibre product, topological inverse image, sheafification, colimit) and names the restriction map explicitly. Mathlib searches of the item were already recorded (all three kinds, no match).
